blocks.text: Appliance Removal Services in Aurora, Ontario — From Renovation-Day Swap-Outs to the Basement Freezer's Farewell

c: In Aurora, appliances rarely die of old age — they get replaced. Kitchens are renovated, builder units give way to built-ins, and perfectly heavy machines suddenly need to leave through hallways that were never consulted. Whether it’s a wall oven coming out mid-renovation, a fridge making way for a panel-ready upgrade, or the chest freezer that’s finally hummed its last, our fully insured crew removes it cleanly: free quote at your door, careful hands on your floors, and the old unit gone — often the same day.

Frequently Asked Questions About Appliance Removal in Aurora, ON

items.q: Q: How is appliance removal priced in Aurora?
a: A: By the truck space the load occupies — starting at $125 for small loads — with the exact flat figure quoted free at your door. A machine’s weight, the stairs involved and the time it takes are all built in, never billed on top, and an approved price can’t change.

items.q: Q: Can you remove a built-in wall oven or panel-ready fridge without damaging the cabinetry?
a: A: That’s precisely the kind of removal we’re set up for. Built-ins come out with the surrounding millwork protected and intact — pads, patience and the right order of operations — so the cabinet opening is ready for the new unit, not a repair quote.

items.q: Q: We're renovating the kitchen — can you time the pickup to demolition day?
a: A: Yes, and we recommend it. Tell us the contractor’s schedule and we’ll clear every retiring appliance in one coordinated visit, leaving the space empty for the trades. One combined load also prices better than several separate pickups.

items.q: Q: Do older Aurora homes with narrow doorways cost more?
a: A: No. Tight halls and heritage-width doorways just mean more careful manoeuvring — doors off hinges, fridge doors off the unit, extra padding on the trim. It’s all standard technique, all included in the volume-based price.

items.q: Q: What has to be disconnected before you arrive?
a: A: Only gas appliances and hardwired units — those need a licensed technician first, for safety and code. Everything with a standard plug or water line (washers, dishwashers, fridges with ice makers) we disconnect ourselves on arrival.
